title: Chapter 37
content:
"Where is he?"

"We haven't located him yet, Father. I have men sweeping every square inch of the vessel."

The heavy, plate-sized palm of Choi Moon-sung swept across the air, striking Choi Ki-tae violently across the cheek. Ki-tae staggered from the impact, yet sprang right back to attention like a weighted punching dummy, locking his hands behind his back at parade rest.

Unable to contain his volcanic fury, Moon-sung delivered a relentless barrage of backhands. Ki-tae’s face rapidly bruised, turning an angry, scalded crimson beneath the heavy blows.

Flanking the master stateroom, the surrounding guards held their breath in terror, not daring to make a sound.

"Incompetent, brainless dogs! You couldn't even corner a single rat!"

"I will drag him to you myself, Father. Please, trust me."

Moon-sung ground his molars together with a sickening crunch. He had been in the middle of a private massage deep within the inner thermal suites when the power suddenly died. At first, he assumed it was a brief generator trip, but the rising commotion in the corridor signaled deliberate sabotage.

Yet when his men breached the hallway, the intruder had evaporated into thin air. One enforcer had been found beaten unconscious on the deck, babbling that the assailant was masked and impossible to identify.

"Did you verify every name on the master registry?"

"Yes, Father. Biometrics, credentials, and full-body pat-downs were conducted without exception."

"Then how the hell did an assassin breach this ship?! Did he sprout wings and fly onto the deck?!"

"My deepest apologies. We will flush him out and execute him immediately."

"Spare me your useless apologies! The guests must not catch wind of this. Ensure the VIPs remain completely insulated from the disturbance."

"Understood."

Several high-profile clients were already sending anxious inquiries to the purser's desk. The syndicate's clientele was already on edge after the devastating explosion at their Doksan-dong processing hub. If another major security failure unfolded tonight, their narcotics empire would collapse overnight, and they would be permanently wiped off the map.

Just then, a detail of enforcers stepped out from Moon-sung's adjoining private quarters.

"The master suite is secure, Chairman."

Moon-sung strode inside, with Ki-tae trailing close behind.

"I will bring you his head, Father. Please, rest easy."

Despite the fierce resolve in his son's voice, Moon-sung’s fury remained white-hot.

The moment Ki-tae exited to direct the manhunt, Moon-sung retrieved a heavy semi-automatic handgun stashed beneath his pillow, placed it on the glass table, and braced both hands against his hips, drawing a deep, ragged breath. Whoever this wretched rat was, the moment he was dragged before him, Moon-sung intended to tear him apart limb from limb before feeding the scraps to the open sea.

Selecting a rich cigar from his case, he sparked the tip and walked over to the porthole. Outside, squads of armed security details moved in tight formations across the illuminated decks.

Crushing the half-smoked cigar into the obsidian tray, he turned around—

His eyes flared in sheer, paralyzing shock.

A suppressed pistol was leveled dead-center between his brows. The intruder was standing bare feet away, having materialized out of thin air without making a whisper of sound.

Moon-sung’s gaze darted up toward the ceiling. The heavy louvered cover of the primary air vent was dangling off its frame. He flicked his eyes back to the entrance—the heavy door that had been open moments ago was latched and bolted tight from within.

Holding the weapon steady, the intruder brought an index finger to his lips.

Hush.

Then, he drew a horizontal line across his own throat—a silent, absolute warning that a single shout meant instant execution.

Moon-sung glared at the assassin, his jaw locked in rigid defiance. Those eyes. Something about that cold, predatory stare struck a chord of recognition.

As Moon-sung stared, the intruder reached up with his free hand and slowly pulled the tactical black mask down past his chin.

The face was unmistakable: the young man from his youngest son’s funeral days ago.

The Hong Kong heir who had been accompanied by Kang Seok-joo.

"Y-You... Why are you—!"

Jakyeong watched the old man with dead, unblinking detachment.

While the vessel's armed security had swarmed the thermal suites below, Jakyeong had slipped through the ventilation network, waiting silently inside the shaft above this very suite. The minutes spent crouched in the dark had felt like an eternity. He had contemplated putting a bullet through the back of the old man's skull the second Ki-tae walked out, but changed his mind—he wanted this monster to see the exact face of the reaper coming for his life.

Keeping his eyes locked on Jakyeong, Moon-sung slowly shifted his right arm, fingertips creeping toward the handgun resting on the table.

The split-second his fingernail brushed the polymer grip, a muted hiss tore from the suppressor. A blinding muzzle flash lit the room.

Moon-sung looked down at his own hand. A fraction of a second later, a wave of white-hot, agonizing torment crashed over his nervous system. He collapsed onto his knees, unable to form a coherent scream.

Three of his fingers had been completely obliterated into red mist and shattered bone.

Gasping for air through ragged, choking breaths, he found the cold steel of Jakyeong’s suppressor pressed firmly against the center of his forehead. Looking up into those brown irises, Moon-sung found a terrifying, bottomless void devoid of a single drop of mercy.

Cold sweat drenched Moon-sung’s face as he glared up at his executioner.

"Who... who the fuck sent you?"

A thin, venomous smile curled the corner of Jakyeong’s lips. "Why? Hoping to seek revenge from beyond the grave?"

"Do you think... you'll walk off this ship alive?!"

"How amusing. Your younger son choked out those exact same words before he died. Is that what Koreans call 'like father, like son'?"

Moon-sung’s eyes dilated in wild, feral horror. "You... you bastard! My boy—!"

"Lee Ja-kyeong."

"What?"

"The name of the man who sent me to kill you."

Before Moon-sung could part his lips to speak, a high-velocity hollow-point tore clean through his forehead, the back of his skull violently erupting outward and painting the silk curtains in a dark, arterial spray.

Moon-sung crashed backward onto the carpet, his lifeless eyes staring frozen at the ceiling.

Jakyeong stood over the corpse with absolute indifference, his trigger finger working in rapid, mechanical rhythm.

One round. Two. Three. Four. Five.

With every flash of the muzzle, the suffocating ghosts of his childhood surged and shattered against the walls. Bone fragments, tissue, and blood rained across the floor.

Only when the old man’s face had been reduced to an unrecognizable, hollowed pulp of crimson gristle did Jakyeong release the trigger. A severed eyeball had rolled free, resting on the carpet, gazing blindly upward.

Jakyeong brought his heel down, grinding the organ into the floorboards until nothing remained.

He yanked the silk duvet from the mattress, swiftly wiping the blood spatter from his hands and face.

Just then, two sharp knocks sounded on the stateroom door.

Jakyeong vaulted off the sofa, hauled his frame up into the open air vent, and pulled the louvered cover back into place. Worming his way through the metal duct, the muffled, urgent voices of crew members echoed from the deck below.

Navigating the narrow conduit with fluid, low-profile crawling, a familiar voice crackled through his encrypted earpiece.

[Jakyeong. What's your position?]

"Still inside the hull. Where are you, Ryun?"

[I made it off the ship and secured the extraction boat. I managed to loop the main security feeds, but the perimeter watch is swarming the waterline. Bringing the boat alongside the hull is suicide right now.]

"Understood. I'll reach the extraction deck as fast as I can."

[Move fast. I'm holding position.]

Reaching the service restroom duct, Jakyeong popped the intake grate and dropped silently onto the tile. He brushed the ventilation dust from his bespoke suit and slid his dark sunglasses back onto his nose. Pressing his shoulder against the door frame, he checked the hallway through the frosted glass panel. Clear.

Stepping into the main corridor, the mezzanine level was in turmoil. Several anxious passengers had stepped out onto the balconies to gauge the security response, while crew members sprinted in every direction trying to maintain order.

Jakyeong moved toward the forward gangway, only to find the ballroom checkpoint heavily fortified with armed guards. Aborting the direct route, he recalled the layout of the tertiary stairwell along the port side of the third deck. He pivoted on his heel, circling the perimeter corridor.

Rounding the final bend, two armed guards turned the corner directly ahead.

Jakyeong offered a curt, polite nod, preparing to glide past them.

He had taken barely four paces when a sharp voice barked behind him.

"Sir. Please halt immediately."

Jakyeong feigned ignorance, accelerating his stride. The heavy, synchronized cadence of their combat boots matched his pace instantly.

"Sir! I said stop!"

The shouts grew louder. Jakyeong ground his teeth.

The unmistakable metallic slide of an assault rifle being chambered echoed down the narrow corridor. Jakyeong stopped in his tracks.

"Final warning. Turn around slowly with your hands where we can see them."

Jakyeong stood motionless, staring down the carpeted hall. The guards were holding a firing angle barely twenty feet behind him. The service hatch was still fifty yards ahead, and to make matters worse, two additional guards patrolling the intersecting corridor had caught the disturbance and were marching toward him.

Jakyeong closed his eyes for a split second.

A gravelly voice broke through the tension from behind the guards. "What's the issue here?"

Damn it all. Choi Ki-tae.

"This guest matches the intruder's general build, boss. He refused to stop."

The heavy, confident strides of Ki-tae approached. Jakyeong’s fingertips buzzed with adrenaline. Even if he drew his sidearm and put a bullet through Ki-tae right now, fighting his way through four armed guards in a closed bottleneck offered zero guarantee of survival.

"I assume you heard the command," Ki-tae said, stepping closer. "Turn around and present your invitation and credentials."

Jakyeong’s hand slowly drifted toward the concealed holster inside his jacket.

A door unlatched right beside him.

The four guards froze mid-stride.

Kang Il-hyun stepped out into the corridor, lowering a smartphone from his ear. His dark, aristocratic features were cool and collected, an eyebrow arching into a sharp, skeptical angle.

Their gazes locked dead-center. Behind his dark lenses, Jakyeong’s pupils contracted violently. Of all the people on this damn ship...

The suffocating silence stretched into an eternity, cold sweat trickling down Jakyeong's spine.

Il-hyun closed the distance between them with long, casual strides, reaching out to clasp Jakyeong’s upper arm in a firm grip. Before Jakyeong could process the contact, Il-hyun smiled with disarming warmth, his fingers gently brushing the side of Jakyeong's cheek.

"What took you so long? I've been waiting for you."

Jakyeong’s breath hitched in his throat.

Behind them, the corridor fell dead silent.

Il-hyun slowly turned his head, his dark eyes fixing onto Choi Ki-tae with frigid detachment.

"Is there a reason you're harassing my guest?"

Ki-tae blinked, thrown completely off balance. "Director Kang... this gentleman is your companion?"

"And if he is?"

"My... my sincerest apologies, sir. We were operating under high alert—we didn't realize he was under your protection."

Il-hyun let out a quiet, mocking scoff, pulled Jakyeong by the arm, and guided him inside the suite.

The heavy door swung shut and latched behind them.

Jakyeong stood rooted to the carpet, unable to move a muscle. He shifted his eyes toward the towering figure before him. The warm, affectionate veneer Il-hyun had shown in the hallway had vanished entirely, replaced by an arctic, calculating gaze looking down from above.

Outside, the footsteps of the security detail faded down the corridor.

In the breathless, heavy silence, Kang Il-hyun was the first to speak.

"Your face looks remarkably familiar."

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut, meeting the stare. Il-hyun was completely composed—almost as if they had agreed to meet in this room all along.

"Why is the little stray cat I left safely at home... roaming aboard an offshore syndicate vessel?"

Il-hyun took two slow, deliberate steps forward, closing the distance until his chest nearly brushed Jakyeong's lapels. The rich, familiar scent of his aftershave was overwhelmingly sharp.

Jakyeong shifted his eyes, taking in the layout of the room. The twin bed was pristine and unoccupied.

Il-hyun raised both hands, planting his palms flat against the door frame on either side of Jakyeong’s head, trapping him completely within his physical space.

The corners of Il-hyun's lips pulled upward into a slow, terrifying smile.

"Care to explain yourself, Yi-an?"

"..."

"Or should I be using your real name?"
